text: In nineteen sixty-two, NASA's first Venus probe was blown up by its own safety officer, less than five minutes after launch.
A handwritten formula for the guidance program was missing one tiny bar over a symbol. That bar meant: smooth the speed data. Without it, the computer reacted to every random jitter.
When the rocket briefly lost its guidance signal, the program started steering it hard. It veered toward the shipping lanes, so they hit self-destruct.
Eighteen and a half million dollars. Arthur C. Clarke called it the most expensive hyphen in history.
Dave was the one who proofread it.
